body.statement:
For design A, \(\mathscr A\) first tests \(m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\) and every structural chart for \(\mathcal C_A(T)\).  If the margin test fails or all charts are empty, then \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)=\varnothing\), and the law is not rigid under \(\lvert\mathcal T_A(p,m)\rvert=1\).  Otherwise the compiler samples \(x_0\in\mathcal C_A(T)\), sets \(t_0=\tau_C(x_0)\), and design A is rigid if and only if every chartwise disagreement set \(V_\chi(t_0)\) in (18) is empty.  For design B, all structural charts are empty if and only if \(\mathcal F_B(p)=\varnothing\); otherwise a sampled \(x_0\in\mathcal C_B(T)\) gives \(t_0\), and design B is rigid if and only if every corresponding residual-forest chartwise disagreement set is empty.  These are finite observable rank, support, incidence, residual-cycle, and exact realizability tests.

For an arbitrary real input \(\zeta\), a rigid \(t_0\) is returned as a rational expression in \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\) only when the compiler constructs such an expression; every other value is returned as a uniquely ordered real element of a finite algebraic extension, encoded by a square-free real-univariate polynomial over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\), rational coordinate functions, and Thom sign data.  For rational \(\zeta\), the representation may be normalized to a square-free integer polynomial and rational isolating interval.  Every nonrigid output contains two legal full SCMs with identical observables and identical supplied margins when margins are supplied, but different \(\tau\).  If both sampled cycle witnesses lie in interior support charts, their full-SCM lifts can be chosen strictly positive; no strict-positivity conclusion is asserted for a witness on a boundary face.
body.justification: The theorem is the necessary-and-sufficient causal classifier, with incompatibility separated from nonrigidity.
body.gap: Regular inversion does not decide global constancy across mixed-rank and boundary charts.
body.consumer: Analysts receive an exact target, legal full-SCM twins, or incompatibility without component enumeration.
body.proof_tex:
For design A, \(\mathrm{lem:design\text{-}a\text{-}fiber\text{-}nonempty\text{-}criterion}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_A(p,m)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 m\in\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}
 \ \hbox{and}\ 
 \mathcal C_A(T)\ne\varnothing.                           \tag{24}
\]
For design B, surjectivity in \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives
\[
 \mathcal F_B(p)\ne\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal C_B(T)\ne\varnothing.                           \tag{25}
\]
The exhaustive chart equalities in \(\mathrm{thm:mixed\text{-}support\text{-}elimination\text{-}complete}\) make nonemptiness of either cycle fiber equivalent to nonemptiness of at least one of its finitely many structural charts.  Equations (24)--(25) therefore prove both incompatibility tests.  Since the cardinality of an empty target set is zero, an incompatible law is not rigid under \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}rigidity}\).

On a nonempty fiber, the same lift lemma preserves the target and is onto, whence
\[
 \mathcal T_A(p,m)
 =\{\tau_C(x):x\in\mathcal C_A(T)\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal T_B(p)
 =\{\tau_C(x):x\in\mathcal C_B(T)\}.                      \tag{26}
\]
The mixed-support theorem proves that the applicable set on the right of (26) is \(\{t_0\}\) exactly when every chartwise disagreement set \(V_\chi(t_0)\) is empty.  Combining this equivalence with \(\mathrm{def:target\text{-}rigidity}\) proves necessity and sufficiency of the stated observable tests.

When every disagreement set is empty, the sample \(x_0\) gives the common target, and the field-expression versus real-univariate/Thom output discipline follows from the exact representation in the mixed-support theorem.  When a disagreement set is nonempty, that theorem returns \(x_0,x_1\) with distinct cycle targets.  Equation (26) and \(\mathrm{lem:cycle\text{-}to\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) yield legal full SCMs with the same observable input and the same supplied \(m\) in design A.  Finally, \(\mathrm{lem:interior\text{-}cycle\text{-}to\text{-}positive\text{-}scm\text{-}lift}\) gives strictly positive lifts precisely under the stated interior-chart premise.  Boundary witnesses remain legal by the general lift, but no unused positivity premise is imposed on them.
